result.summary: This PR implements the headers presync parameter optimization algorithm directly in C++, computing commitment period and redownload buffer sizes at node startup based on chain age and minchainwork height. It removes hardcoded headers-sync parameters from chainparams and deletes the offline Python generation script. Unit tests and fuzz tests are added to verify solver correctness and termination.
result.problem: Headers presync DoS parameters were previously generated offline by an ad-hoc Python script and hardcoded into chain parameters for each release, requiring maintainer intervention and leaving nodes running old software with degrading DoS margins over time.

resolved_concerns: ajtowns questioned whether runtime clock values could leak node timing via parameters; sipa showed values change only once every ~22 days during IBD
shuv-amp identified infinite loops in the solver for small minchainwork heights and zero timespans, which sipa fixed with bounded loops and fuzz tests
darosior noted the batch-of-2000 model in Python and initial C++ underestimated attacks where attackers abort mid-batch; sipa addressed this by switching to a simpler single-header arrival model
discussion.author_status: active, recently reworked the algorithm to use a simpler continuous model and force-pushed updates

result.card: This PR moves the computation of headers presync DoS parameters (commitment period and redownload buffer size) from an offline Python script committed to chainparams to an on-the-fly startup calculation in C++. This eliminates a manual maintainer task during release cycles and prevents defense degradation as the chain grows past software release dates. Support is strong with Concept ACKs from multiple contributors and an Approach ACK from ajtowns; earlier concerns regarding convergence and attack models were resolved in recent pushes. It is ready for review.
